caption: The drawing depicts a single, vertically-oriented object that appears to be a tooled leather item, possibly a sheath or decorative covering. The object is predominantly reddish-brown with varying shades of darker and lighter brown to create depth and contour. The surface is adorned with an embossed or carved floral or leaf-like pattern, with large, rounded, petal-shaped motifs radiating from central points. The border of the object features a repeating diamond or triangular motif along a narrow band, adding further detail. The object's asymmetric, slightly curved shape widens at the top and tapers towards the bottom. The background is plain and off-white, and the only visible text “HARRY MANU WADDELL” is located near the lower right corner of the image in small handwriting.
title: Gun Holster
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
